extracted.intended_audience: new college mathematics instructors / graduate student instructors (GSIs) and course instructors
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and procedural standards for instructors (especially new instructors/GSIs) on handling end-of-semester tasks: exams, grading, communicating grades, cheating, complaints, and related meetings. Also includes conflict-management and feedback techniques for difficult instructor–student interactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Steps in the Feedback Process
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) Describe the problem or situation to the student. (b) Define what feelings or reactions you have towards the behavior. (c) Suggest a solution, or ask the student to provide a solution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Central idea: deal with situations as quickly as you can. Feedback identifies what another person has done that annoys/upsets you, tells the person exactly what it is, and then gives the person an opportunity to do something about it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be sure the student is ready (feedback timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure the student is prepared to receive feedback; if distracted, resentful, or eager to leave, it may not be the right time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the student appears distracted, seems very resentful of being taken aside, or keeps asking questions like, 'Is this going to take long? I really have to be somewhere else,' then delay feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Base feedback on facts, not emotions
rubrics_metrics.description: When giving feedback, ground comments in observable facts rather than emotional judgments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid vague or emotionally loaded statements; use specific behaviors as evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be as specific as you can (feedback content)
rubrics_metrics.description: Point to specific instances of the student's behavior rather than making vague generalizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific examples have a much more dramatic impact than vague statements like 'It bothers me when you talk in class.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Give feedback as soon after the event as possible
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide feedback close in time to the incident so the student can recall the behavior addressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The closer in time the feedback, the more likely the student will remember details and act on it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Find a private place to give feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid delivering highly critical feedback in front of others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public criticism can be more damaging than helpful; seek privacy when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concentrate on what the student can change
rubrics_metrics.description: Focus feedback on behaviors or actions within the student's control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid criticizing traits or things the student cannot realistically change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request the student's cooperation
rubrics_metrics.description: Ask the student to help make class a better learning environment by reconsidering their behavior choices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame feedback as a cooperative effort to improve the classroom for everyone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on one thing at a time (feedback scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: Address a single behavior or issue rather than overwhelming the student with many points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presenting too much information can leave the student confused and upset.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding short-term conflict avoidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not automatically take the path of least resistance; short-term solutions (e.g., conceding to a belligerent student's demand) may create long-term problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider long-term consequences when deciding whether to avoid or engage with conflict (e.g., granting extra work to one student may create pressure for others).

rubrics_metrics.name: Adversarial Action (cause of conflict)
rubrics_metrics.description: When disagreements are seen as 'win-lose,' parties treat issues as battles for autonomy or authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In instructor–student contexts this mindset makes behavior change harder because parties view the interaction as something to be won or lost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tightly Held Positions (cause of conflict)
rubrics_metrics.description: People harden their positions and limit involvement; they don't see a need to achieve goals together.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students may refuse to see behavior as inappropriate if they interpret correction as a moral judgment; instructors should frame behavior change as pragmatic and nonjudgmental.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotional Involvement (cause of conflict)
rubrics_metrics.description: People become attached to positions/methods, making it hard to address problems rationally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both students and instructors may be emotionally invested; instructors should be aware of their own emotional triggers and manage them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructor direct confrontation (emotional reaction anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructor decides to confront directly but comes across as aggressive; student may respond similarly and escalate the conflict.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be mindful that intended frankness can be perceived as aggression; adjust tone and approach accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructor indirect manipulation (emotional reaction anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructor handles issues indirectly (e.g., concocting situations to make the student look bad) rather than addressing behavior openly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This approach is manipulative and unprofessional; avoid it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Postponing/avoiding response (emotional reaction anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructor tolerates behavior hoping the semester will end and the problem will disappear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delaying response can worsen long-term outcomes; address issues proactively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Giving in (emotional reaction anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructor treats inappropriate behavior as acceptable rather than addressing it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid passive acceptance which undermines standards and classroom environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferred responses to conflict
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct energies toward solving difficulties and respond rationally even to emotional students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on solutions, keep interactions professional, and avoid emotional escalation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Six steps for confronting and resolving conflict
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) Acknowledge conflict exists. (b) Identify the real reason. (c) Each party presents point of view and listens. (d) Explore solutions both can live with. (e) Agree on a solution. (f) Instructor follows up to ensure it works.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both parties must listen without interrupting; potential solutions must be acceptable to both parties; follow-up is essential to verify effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Goals for the end-of-semester meeting
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide instructors with administrative details, clarify responsibilities, allow Q&A, give ideas for dealing with cheating and grade complaints, explain grading scheme, give checklist for exam information, and (optionally) demonstrate final-grade calculations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meeting should be 30–50 minutes, primarily targeted at new instructors; optional demonstration of final-grade calculation may lengthen meeting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation for the end-of-semester meeting
rubrics_metrics.description: Gather institutional/departmental grading guidelines, adapt handouts, modify calendar, create grade-reporting flow chart, collect official forms, prepare demonstration materials if needed, circulate agenda, and make copies/confirm attendance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bring or prepare materials that reflect your institution's conventions; circulate agenda in advance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agenda items for the meeting
rubrics_metrics.description: Suggested agenda includes: before the final exam (scheduling reviews, exam info, alternate exams, instructor commitments), final exam day (proctoring, room security), cheating, submitting grades, pass/fail/incompletes, communicating grades, handling complaints, changing grades, post-semester responsibilities, and determining final grades (optional).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider each item carefully; customize to institutional relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outline for running the meeting (timing and content)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suggested minute-by-minute outline: :01–:05 intro; :05–:15 distribute handouts and clarify responsibilities; :15–:20 summarize exam proctoring; :20–:30 explain grade reporting procedure; :30–:35 describe non-standard grades; :35–:45 describe returning exams and grading systems; :45–:50 wrap up; optional demonstration of grade calculations may follow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make explicit, unequivocal statements of responsibilities; promise to follow up on unanswered questions and do so.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meeting materials to provide
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide copies of institutional guidelines, the 'Administrative Issues for the End of Semester' handout, calendar of important jobs/dates, flow chart of grade reporting, and optional handouts/slides for grade calculation demonstration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Materials should be adapted to your institution and distributed in advance when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scheduling review sessions (administrative)
rubrics_metrics.description: Request rooms early from secretarial staff as room requests can take up to a week to fill during exam period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan ahead given high demand during exams.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information to communicate to students before the final
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly communicate date/time/location of final exam, essential items students must bring, allowable special items, and the grading scheme for calculating final grades.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tell every student; make sure they are aware of alternate exam procedures if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternate exam policy and notification
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide alternate exams for students with conflicts (another exam at same time or four+ exams in one day); notify course director if students need an alternate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate alternate exams with course director and plan logistics in advance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proctoring requirement and exam-room procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructors are required to proctor their final exam to identify section students, ensure fairness for special-needs students, and handle missing/late students. Take attendance, record present/excused/missing students, accept only exams from students in your section, check names off, and inspect room for discarded papers before leaving.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These steps protect students and instructors; collaborate with other instructors if papers seem miscollected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cheating detection and reporting protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: If suspected cheating, consult another instructor; if consensus, gather all instructors to observe; prepare a written case (photocopies, testimonies, your account) and use official departmental channels to report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be sure of misconduct before acting; many innocent behaviors can look like cheating; avoid 'home-made justice'—use official procedures to protect both parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Before submitting grades (reflection and documentation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Decide and be able to articulate why each grade is assigned, especially in borderline cases; think through reasons to reduce stress and to prepare for possible complaints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Writing out reasons clarifies decisions and helps respond to student complaints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submitting grades (procedural)
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit official grade reports on official sheets to the Registrar/department as instructed; make a photocopy for your records; if leaving town, sign the sheet and entrust it to a trusted colleague.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow deadlines and departmental memos for where/when to turn in reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy on non-standard grades (I, X, NR)
rubrics_metrics.description: I (Incomplete), X (excused absence), and NR (no report) should be rare; I is only for missing portion of work and cannot be used if student completed all work; X is for missing final/alternate with satisfactory excuse and given in consultation with course director; NR when student never attended or only early term attendance; these lapse to E unless changed by deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not alter preprinted special-grade codes on official sheets; consult course director for nonstandard situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pass–fail student grading policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute and record pass–fail students' grades as usual; the Registrar will convert to pass/fail. Knowing who is pass–fail should not affect grading decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat pass–fail students identically to others when grading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Returning papers and precautions
rubrics_metrics.description: Options: mail (student provides stamped, self-addressed envelope) or in-person pick-up; do not leave exams in public places; once exam leaves your custody, no further score changes can be made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protect exam security to prevent theft/alteration; set clear terms about further score changes when returning exams.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communicating grades (privacy rules and methods)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not post grades (federal privacy rules); departmental offices do not give out grades; do not release grade information to anyone except the student (parents/guardians not entitled). Options include stamped/self-addressed envelope, scheduled office hours, or email (with student consent via writing on exam).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe privacy regulations and ensure only the student receives their grade.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparing for and handling grade complaints
rubrics_metrics.description: Prevent complaints by keeping excellent records, using a rational, uniformly-applied grading system, and having clear reasons for grade assignments. If complaints occur, be ready to explain reasons and show objective criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most complaints disappear when you show grades were assigned uniformly and objectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Being ready for complaints (what to demonstrate)
rubrics_metrics.description: Be able to give specific reasons for the grade (especially borderline cases), demonstrate objective criteria were used and applied uniformly, explain the decision within two minutes, and avoid digressing into broader philosophies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preparation reduces confrontations and helps resolve disputes quickly and professionally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common student arguments and recommended responses
rubrics_metrics.description: Typical lines: 'I require a certain grade to achieve X' (reply: grades assigned in same way; advise academic advisor), 'Extra work to make up grade?' (firm NO — equal treatment for all), 'Can I see the curve? I'm one point away?' (you may decline regrading; state your judgment), 'Credit for trying/improvement?' (respond based on objective criteria).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistent, firm, and uniform answers prevent unfair exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling belligerent students
rubrics_metrics.description: If a student is combative and will not accept answers, end the meeting and arrange for the student (and/or you) to meet with the course director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After the meeting, write down, to the best of your recollection, exactly what was said during the interview.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responding to attempted bribery or improper conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: If you feel a student is attempting to bribe you, terminate the interview immediately, remove the student from your office, find a trusted witness, write down exactly what happened, and contact the course director as soon as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although rare, treat even joking references to bribery seriously and document the interaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changing grades (policy and procedure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Grade changes are made via an official change-of-grade form. The only official reasons are to correct clerical errors or to replace a grade of I or X. For other cases, consult the course director before making changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the policy as a firm and unequivocal reply to students requesting grade changes; think carefully before assigning grades initially.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-semester responsibilities (exam retention)
rubrics_metrics.description: If students do not pick up their exams, retain exams for one year after the date of the final.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain records and physical exams safely for the retention period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official breakdown and formulas for calculating final grades
rubrics_metrics.description: Example official breakdown: Exam 1 15%, Exam 2 20%, Final Exam 25%, Homework 25%, In-Class Work & Quizzes 15%. Weighted uniform exam score W = 0.15*S1 + 0.2*S2 + 0.25*SF. Final weighted total ST = W + 15*(Q/150) + 25*(H/300).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uniform exam scores (W) range 0–60. Homework and quiz grade ranges are selected by plotting cumulative scores and choosing cutoffs so the distribution of letter grades matches the distribution from uniform grades. For final grade lower bounds (e.g., A), combine the weighted lower bounds from each component according to their weight (example: 0.1 = 15/150 times quiz lower bound, 0.0833 = 25/300 times homework lower bound, etc.). Use fictitious or pseudonymized data for demonstrations and include borderline cases during demonstrations but avoid excessive detail that confuses participants.
